title: Part Seventeen: Families Through the Machine

sections.brief: BLS CE 2024 quintile budgets (no personas): definitions (consumer unit, means, mortgage principal and loan repayments excluded from spending, SS deductions in personal insurance and pensions, 2024 after-tax income not published, tax estimated from 2023 ratios); middle fifth $74,474 -> taxes $9,412 (12.6%) -> spending $60,652 -> left $4,410 (5.9%), ~$2,900 uncommitted; fourth fifth $121,548 -> $21,222 -> $78,038 -> $22,288 (18.3%); lowest and second fifths spend 2.1x and 1.17x reported income; SCF 2025 median net worth by usual-income band ($14.4k/$77.1k/$188.2k/$362.5k); ITEP all-tax rates and CBO federal rates; EITC/CTC/SNAP and cliff; three shocks with arithmetic (deductible $1,955 = 44% of margin, OOP max $10,600 = 2.4 years; job loss gap ~$5,440; rent +10% = $1,837, +29% = $4,130); 2020-2024 margins by fifth; where it works (fourth fifth); told vs record. Figures: compare (four fifths); money (middle family's year); flow (three shocks); compare (told vs record)

Life script at documented medians, each stage linked to its mechanism part: childcare $6,552-15,600 (2022) and CCDF 7% cap repealed July 2026; school $17,619/pupil, $11,060-$31,918, 43.2% local, Rodriguez, Ed Trust vs Urban; college $25,850 COA, net tuition $2,300, Pell 27.2%, 47% borrow avg $29,560, $1.65tn, 7.7m default, garnishment status 19 Oct 2026; first job $802/$1,173 weekly (Q3 2026), payroll, single premium, auto-enrolment; rent $1,531 vs $61,240 needed, 49% burdened; median new home $410,700 at 7.40% = $2,559/mo, 35.1% of median income, under-35 ownership 35.2%, NAR age 40 caveat; health premiums, underinsured 23%, PTC expiry; SCF debt and net worth by age; 401(k) 54.9%/$106k/$44,115; Social Security $2,088 -> $2,163, 2034/83%, poverty 9.9% official vs 15.4% SPM; where it works; labelled tollgate interpretation with counter-readings. Figures: flow (life script); money (first paycheck); stats (mortgage); compare (told vs record)
